question.problem: Consider the triangle $C$ in the plane with vertices $(-1,0),(1,0)$ and $(-1,2),$ and the region $D$ bounded by $C.$ Express ${∮}_{C}({y}^{2}-2xy)\,dx+(x\operatorname{sin}⁡y-{x}^{2})\,dy$ as a repeated integral.
question.worked_solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first partial derivatives on an open region containing $D$, then Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dx+Q\,dy={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14120089/assets/eac7a442f0a794db0606b95aa722320d099f2bcc4e530fc6b62e9be889335da2.png)

 

We have that $P(x,y)={y}^{2}-2xy$ and $Q(x,y)=x\operatorname{sin}⁡y-{x}^{2}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂y}=2y-2x,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡y-2x.\end{aligned}
$$

We can express the region $D$ as a type I region as follows:

$$
D={(x,y):-1\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 1-x}
$$

Therefore, applying Green's Theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}({y}^{2}-2xy)\,dx+(x\operatorname{sin}⁡y-{x}^{2})\,dy & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}[\operatorname{sin}⁡y-2x-(2y-2x)]\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(\operatorname{sin}⁡y-2y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{1-x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡y-2y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$
